record.original_question: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions for a discrete subset of the positive real numbers R^+ to occur as the spectrum of the Laplacian on some compact manifold.

evidence.quote: What is the necessary and sufficient condition for a set of discrete numbers in R^+ to be the spectrum of the Laplacian of some compact manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold (without boundary), and let $\Delta_g$ denote the (non-negative) Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions on $M$. It is classical that the spectrum of $\Delta_g$ consists of a discrete sequence
$$0 = \lambda_0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \lambda_3 \le \cdots \to \infty$$
of eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity), each of finite multiplicity.

Problem. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on a discrete subset (or sequence) $S \subset \mathbb{R}^+$ that characterize when $S$ arises as the Laplace spectrum of some smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. In other words, give an intrinsic characterization (in terms of the sequence $S$ alone, without reference to a manifold) of those discrete sets of positive real numbers that occur as $\{\lambda_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ for some compact Riemannian manifold equipped with its Laplace–Beltrami operator.
artifact.status_search_result: A general intrinsic characterization of which discrete subsets of $\mathbb{R}^+$ arise as Laplace spectra of compact Riemannian manifolds is not known. Only partial results exist: Weyl's law gives an asymptotic necessary condition, heat-kernel and wave-trace invariants supply further constraints, and isospectral but non-isometric examples (Milnor 1964; Sunada; Gordon–Webb–Wolpert) show the spectrum-to-geometry map is highly non-injective. No survey identifies a solution to the inverse-existence problem, which remains an open question in spectral geometry.

status_evidence.title: The Spectrum of the Laplacian in Riemannian Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known constraints (Weyl law, heat invariants) and isospectral non-isometric examples; no characterization of admissible spectra is provided.
status_evidence.claim: No general necessary and sufficient conditions are known for a sequence to be a Laplace spectrum.

status_evidence.title: Notes for Analysis on Manifolds via the Laplacian (Canzani)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes describe known partial spectral invariants (dimension, volume, total scalar curvature via heat kernel asymptotics) but state that determining all such invariants is open.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial necessary conditions are known.

status_evidence.title: Weyl law - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Weyl's law gives the asymptotic counting function $N(\lambda) \sim C_n \mathrm{Vol}(M)\lambda^{n/2}$, a necessary condition on any Laplace spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Weyl's law gives only a necessary asymptotic condition.
